content:
Reading the documentation for grind, and I don't understand how it handles propositional implications. Is it this part?
https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/The--grind--tactic/Constraint-Propagation/#grind-propagation
If so, where does implication come in?

unxy:
I'm trying to get an idea of how expensive it is for grind to work with theorems of the form
A → B → C when doing backwards reasoning (E-matching on C).

Yes it is the constrant propagator, there is a propgator called propagateForallPropDown that handles this type of stuff. grind uses two indices to determine what to propgate on. There is an index to determine which expressions are affected by something changing in the equivalence class structure and an index to determine which propagators are worth running based on the head symbol of the propagator. propagateForallPropDown is a slight exception here in that it doesn't have a head symbol per-se (after all it starts with a forallE not with a const application) so one can just always try to run it.

So I would say it's pretty cheap^^
